title: Cluster description
description: What one cluster provides, stated once and split across two files. sites/<site>.yaml holds what every cluster of that site has in common; sites/<site>/<cluster>.yaml holds what makes this cluster itself. Both are checked against THIS schema -- a site file is a partial cluster description -- and hpcrun/sitegen merges them before generating anything, so the flat block a job sources is unchanged by the split. Merge rules: a scalar takes the cluster's value, a list takes the site's entries then the cluster's, a map merges key by key with the cluster winning. The rules that decide whether a MERGED description is complete are in benchlib/sitefile.py, not here, because neither file alone can satisfy them.

schema.description: Format version of this file. Bumped only for a change that an older hpcrun/sitegen would misread.

site.description: The site this belongs to. In a site file it names the file itself; in a cluster file it names the parent, and is what sitegen merges with.

description.description: What this machine is, for whoever reads a results directory a year from now. Copied into the generated block as a comment.

verified.description: False means nothing here has been confirmed by a job that actually ran. hpcrun/validate says so out loud rather than letting an untested description pass for a measured one.

scheduler.description: Which batch system, and how a job reaches it.

kind.description: Selects sites/<site>/job.tmpl's directive dialect. Only pbspro is exercised today; slurm is named so the enum rejects a typo rather than accepting an unimplemented value silently.

submit.description: The submission command, qsub or sbatch.

queue.description: Default queue. An experiment's defaults.queue overrides it, and so does HPCRUN_QUEUE in the environment.

place.description: The scheduler's placement policy, emitted as its own directive because it is job-wide rather than per-chunk -- PBS spells it `-l place=scatter:excl`. Distinct from node.select, which describes ONE chunk and cannot express `spread these chunks across distinct hosts and let nobody else on them`. Omit it where the queue's default is already what you want: Derecho's main queue allocates whole nodes, so only a queue that does not needs this stated.

walltime_max.description: The longest walltime this queue accepts. hpcrun/validate refuses a longer request at submit time instead of letting the scheduler reject it after the fact.

modules.description: The module environment, which is the one thing every job here must do identically and the thing that was copied into five PBS scripts before this file existed.

bootstrap.description: The module commands every job runs first, in order, as the body of bench_site_modules. A list rather than one string because order is the whole content: `module reset` after loading ncarenv is not redundant, since ncarenv changes MODULEPATH and reset then applies the defaults visible under the new path.

compiler_map.description: Container compiler tag to host module. The host MPI that displaces the container's must be built with a compatible compiler, and the tag in the image name is the only thing naming which.

^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$.description: The module to load, version and all. Pin the version where the container's compiler must be matched exactly rather than followed.

mpi_map.description: Container MPI family to host module. An empty value means the host MPI is already in the default environment and there is nothing to load -- Cray MPICH on Derecho -- which is not the same as the family being unsupported.

^(openmpi|mpich|mpich3)$.description: The module that provides the host MPI for this container family. Empty means there is nothing to load.

unload_when.description: Modules to drop for a given MPI family, because a module left loaded by a previous image shadows this one. Dropping openmpi before an mpich image is the case that exists: its mpiexec and its libraries would otherwise displace Cray PALS and the MPICH ABI shim.

^(openmpi|mpich|mpich3)$.description: Modules unloaded before this family's is loaded.

node.description: What one compute node has. FALLBACKS, not measurements: the job probes lscpu and topology.json carries its answer. These are what can be known before there is a node to ask, which is the only moment an illegal ranks x threads is still cheap to reject.

ncpus.description: CPUs per node the scheduler will actually hand out -- PBS's resources_available.ncpus -- which can be fewer than the hardware has: Casper's high-throughput Genoa nodes have 64 cores and offer 62, its Cascade Lake nodes 36 and offer 34. The geometry check still reasons in hardware cores; this is what a request may ask for. An exclusive job asks for exactly this many, and hpcrun/validate refuses a cell that needs more, because a request no node can satisfy does not fail -- it queues forever. Omit it where the two are equal.

sockets.description: Populated sockets per node. Used to derive cores per socket, which is the granularity a rank should not straddle.

smt_stride.description: Under a block SMT layout, the sibling of CPU c is c + stride. Equal to cores on a machine that enumerates all first siblings before any second.

cores_per_l3.description: Cores sharing one last-level cache -- a CCD on AMD. Never inferred from a placement report: a run that does not fill a node touches only part of each CCD and would under-count, then declare the result optimal.

cores_per_numa.description: Cores in one NUMA domain. On a machine with NPS4 this is a quarter of a socket, not the whole one.

target_arch.description: The instruction set this hardware actually runs, in the spelling report_cpu_features prints. Checked against the app binary once at job start, which turns a SIGILL on every rank three hours into a queue into one line before the first cell. Deliberately a check and not an input: the image was built in CI long before this file was read, so a site can only refuse to measure an image, never change it.

select.description: Scheduler resource clauses that ask for THIS node type, appended to the select directive -- on Casper, cpu_type=genoa. Without it a description says what the hardware is but not how to obtain it, which is worse than saying nothing because it looks authoritative: the first Casper run named no processor and landed on a node type the file did not describe. Use only resources that steer node CHOICE. A node's queue-eligibility tag is not one of them: on a system with a routing queue, selecting on it fights the router rather than directing it.

topology.description: probe means lscpu on the compute node is the authority and the values above are only a last resort. declared means trust them, which is for a machine where lscpu is not available or not truthful.

container.description: How a container is run here. The bind list is site-specific in the strongest sense: apptainer treats a missing bind source as fatal, so binding a filesystem this machine does not have turns 'that mount is absent' into 'the job will not start'.

binds.description: Bound unconditionally. Only paths this machine is guaranteed to have.

binds_if_present.description: Bound only when the directory exists. Where a filesystem belongs when some nodes have it and some do not -- GPFS and the Cray trees.

bind_map.description: host path to in-container path, for a directory that must not land on top of the container's own. /usr/lib64 is the case: bound at its own name it would replace the container's entire system library tree.

^/[^ ]*$.description: Where the host path appears inside the container.

lib_dirs.description: Host library directories put on LD_LIBRARY_PATH inside the container, in this order, after whatever the MPI overlay prepends. An entry containing * is a glob and resolves to its newest match, because a hardcoded version number rots at the next system update and the job would then silently fall back to the container's own library. An entry may begin ${VAR}/ to name a directory a module supplies, and drops out when that variable is unset. A directory that does not exist is dropped rather than left empty: an empty element in LD_LIBRARY_PATH means the working directory.

images.description: The images this cluster runs, stated as axes rather than as a list: every compiler crossed with every MPI family, on one OS. hpcrun/sitegen turns it into sites/<site>/<cluster>/images.mk, which sif/Makefile includes, so `make <cluster>` builds the base set and `make <cluster>-<app>` each app set; an experiment's images.set names the same sets. A cluster file only: a site file carrying it is refused, because two clusters of one site rarely want the same images and a list inherited from the site would be concatenated, not replaced.

os.description: The container OS, the first word of every image name. The one closest to the host's own userspace -- leap for Derecho's SLE 15.

compilers.description: Container compiler tags. Each must be a key of modules.compiler_map: the host MPI that displaces the container's is loaded to match the compiler, so a compiler with no host module is an image no job here can run.

mpi.description: Container MPI families. Each must be listed under mpi:, which is what says this cluster can host it -- why Casper's set has no mpich.

apps.description: Apps built on top of the base set, one set of images each: <os>-<compiler>-<mpi>-<app>.sif, named <cluster>-<app>.

mpi.description: One entry per container MPI family this site can host. A family absent here is one this machine cannot run, which the runner reports as such rather than attempting and failing inside the container.

^(openmpi|mpich|mpich3)$.description: How this site hosts one container MPI family: which mpiexec dialect places its ranks, which recipe swaps the host library in, and anything that has to be set inside the container for it.

launcher.description: Which mpiexec dialect emits this family's placement flags. PALS spells procs-per-node -ppn N and binding --cpu-bind core -d D; Open MPI spells the same two things -N N and --map-by ppr:P:node:pe=D --bind-to core.

overlay.description: Which recipe in hpcrun/lib/make_apptainer_launcher.sh swaps the host MPI in. A NAME, not a description: the recipe body encodes reasoning -- which of Cray's two library directories carries the MPICH ABI, why OPAL_PREFIX must be pinned -- and reasoning does not belong in a data file.

root.description: Where the host MPI is installed, for an overlay that binds the whole tree -- host-openmpi, which also pins OPAL_PREFIX to it. Usually `${NAME}` for a variable the MPI module sets, single-quoted in the YAML like a lib_dirs entry, and expanded only once that module is loaded. Required by host-openmpi.

env.description: Environment set inside the container for this family. Where a workaround whose reason is specific to this machine goes.

^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$.description: The value, passed through to --env as it is written.

notes.description: Free text. What was checked, and what would make it stop being true.

cluster.description: The cluster: the name an experiment selects with `cluster:`, the directory holding its cluster.sh, and the value recorded in every result row beside the site. Its presence is what distinguishes a cluster file from a site file.

subclusters.description: Node types within this cluster. Casper has seven processor types and Derecho's GPU partition differs from its CPU nodes, so one node: block cannot describe either machine. Each entry states its node: IN FULL -- nothing is inherited from another entry, because a geometry key a node type forgot to state would otherwise silently take a different node's value -- and a cluster with sub-clusters has no top-level node: at all. default_subcluster names the one used when an experiment names none. hpcrun/sitegen emits every entry into cluster.sh, and HPCRUN_SUBCLUSTER, set when the profile is sourced, chooses between them.

^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$.description: One node type: a description of it, and its own node: block.

verified.description: False means no job has yet run on this node type. hpcrun/validate says so, as it does for an unverified cluster.
